correctness.rationale: For all m>=2 and p,q in (0,1), exact reduction to subset tests is proved both ways; finite exact verification checks 40960 profiles. A strong law gives margins m(1-p)q^k-p(m-k), convexity of k log(q)-log(m-k) selects only endpoint coalitions, and Hoeffding yields exponential off-critical convergence. The univariate CLT proves the ordinary boundary 1/2; a bivariate CLT with correlation sqrt(2/(m+1)) gives the exceptional arcsine limit. Marginal and covariance calculations were reconstructed, and the three-candidate value is 3/8. The checker is supplemental rather than an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 study defines the approval-weighted veto core and analyzes deterministic veto thresholds, but the inspected materials do not give a fixed-candidate independent-Bernoulli acceptance phase diagram or the simultaneous-critical arcsine probability. The earlier proportional-veto-core impartial-culture theorem concerns a different rule without an approval gate and uniform strict rankings. Searches of primary literature, the research-record index, and accessible own-claim history recovered no same-object statement or broader theorem implying the new result. The first-source full document has not been examined in every section, so coverage is best-knowledge qualified.

value.rationale: The AWVC mechanism balances majority support and protection against coordinated disapprovers. Quantifying the exact high-population acceptance boundary for independent binary approvals distinguishes two endogenous ways in which this balance can fail and supplies a meaningful calibration for heterogeneous focal-versus-rival approval rates. The double-critical 3/8 probability is a specific nontrivial covariance effect, not a generic approval-score threshold.
